turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um, I'm here because... well, I spend most of my day going back over the same things in the house. The outlets, the locks, my tools, even the dust. I just keep checking and fixing them, again and again. I do it until I'm completely worn out, but... I still just don't feel sure enough to leave it alone.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes spending most of their day repeatedly checking and fixing outlets, locks, tools, and dust in an excessive manner they cannot leave alone, clearly representing checking and repeating compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: What do you fear might happen if you leave something unchecked or imperfect?
turns.patient_response: Well, it's... it's these ugly thoughts that just keep jumping into my head. Even when I know for a fact I did a job right, I'll start thinking that maybe I missed a loose wire and it's going to burn the whole house down. Or... or that I left a stray nail laying around somewhere and my wife is going to step on it and get badly hurt. I try really hard to just push the thoughts out of my mind, but... they just come right back, and they feel even stronger.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes intrusive, distressing thoughts of catastrophic harm (house burning down, wife getting hurt) that persist and return stronger despite active efforts to suppress them.

turns.doctor_question: Do you check mainly to relieve the anxiety caused by these unwanted thoughts?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, that's exactly it. Like I was saying when we first started talking, that's why I spend most of my day going back over the same stuff... the outlets, the locks, my tools, the dust. The anxiety gets so bad from those thoughts, and checking is the only way to get a break from it. 

I just keep checking and fixing things again and again. I'll do it until I'm completely worn out, just to get some relief from the panic... even though, like I said, I still never really feel sure enough to just leave it alone.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive checking and fixing behaviors (locks, outlets, tools, dust) repeatedly until worn out to get relief from severe anxiety and unwanted thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: Do you generally see your need for order, perfection, and control as a natural and desirable part of who you are?
turns.patient_response:
No, definitely not. Um... I don't see it as a good thing at all. There's nothing desirable about spending my whole day checking things. I actually hate living like this. 

I know it's not normal to be this obsessed with everything being perfect or safe, and it's definitely not who I want to be. I don't want to be doing any of this... I just feel like I have to, to stop those bad thoughts.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient reports being obsessed with everything being perfect or safe and experiencing distressing 'bad thoughts' that they feel compelled to stop.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes spending their whole day checking things and feeling compelled to do so to prevent bad thoughts, despite not wanting to.
